his_statement: Positive roots; simple reflection permutes other positive roots; all reflections found.
statement: Every inward normal to a mirror is a nonnegative combination of simple normals. A simple reflection permutes the positive normals other than its own. The G-stable generating mirror set is all mirrors, and |G| equals the chamber count.

his_statement: Closed chamber fundamental domain; point stabilizers generated by mirrors through point.
statement: For a finite real reflection group, each orbit meets a closed chamber in exactly one point. Intersections of chamber closures are closed faces; a point stabilizer is generated by reflections whose mirrors contain the point. The element carrying a chamber is unique, but g in x=g(y) need not be unique on a boundary.
computation: Source cites prior face/coxeter lemmas; the distinction between unique y and nonunique g read directly. No erroneous uniqueness of g is inferred.
fate: Classical chamber/Coxeter structure; modern Bourbaki chapterV confirms subject/edition metadata, while Coxeter1934 provides the underlying fundamental-domain construction.

his_statement: Proper affine reflection groups split orthogonally.
statement: For a discrete group of affine orthogonal isometries generated by affine reflections acting properly on finite-dimensional Euclidean E, the linear parts fix W′ pointwise, all displacements lie in W=(W′)^⊥, and an invariant orthogonal decomposition splits G into the corresponding reflection subgroups. A fixed factor is retained when G is not essential.
computation: Every reflecting normal lies in one invariant summand; its reflection acts trivially on the other, so independent generators give the product surjection.
fate: Coxeter1934 Lemma5.1 and Theorem6 give the classical decomposition.

his_statement: Éliminer les hypothèses affines; les exposés XI, XII, XV, XVI devraient être complètement refondus.
statement: Some maximal-torus and Cartan conclusions extend beyond affine group schemes. For a smooth separated finite-type group scheme G/S admitting maximal tori fpqc locally, SGA3 XII7.1(a,b) gives the torus–Cartan correspondence and étale-local conjugacy. Local constancy of reductive rank alone is not sufficient in the nonaffine case, as XII7.7(a) explicitly warns.
